# Submission Notes

Collaborators: none
Additional resources used: course materials; ggplot2 documentation (https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org); data source: Mirzakhani et al. (2016), GSE85307, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27841759/
This file makes all figures and the summary table. The figures (folder `figures/`) and the
table (`table1.tex`) are uploaded to Overleaf, where the final report is written.

# Packages and seed

```{r packages}
library(ggplot2)    # all plots except the heatmap
library(ggpubr)     # ggarrange(): put plots together in panels A, B, C
library(pheatmap)   # heatmap with clustering and tracking bars
library(knitr)      # kable(): LaTeX table

# Seed so the random jitter in the boxplot is the same every time
set.seed(103)

# Folder for the figure files that go to Overleaf
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Load and wrangle the data

All wrangling starts from the original files provided on Canvas (the three .csv files must be
in the same folder as this .Rmd).

```{r load-data}
# Read the csv files
covar <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar.csv", check.names = FALSE)
expr  <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv", check.names = FALSE)
genes_link <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv", colClasses = "character")

# The first column of the expression file has the probe IDs: use them as row names
rownames(expr) <- expr[[1]]
expr <- expr[, -1]

# Remove the label before ": " (e.g. "age_years: 31.06" -> "31.06")
for (v in names(covar)[3:ncol(covar)]) {
  covar[[v]] <- sub("^[^:]*: ", "", covar[[v]])
}

# Change the continuous covariates from text to numbers
num_vars <- c("mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks", "sampleCollection_gestAge_wks",
              "mat_BMI", "mat_vitD")
for (v in num_vars) {
  covar[[v]] <- as.numeric(covar[[v]])
}

# Match covariates to the expression columns using geoID
covar <- covar[match(colnames(expr), covar$geoID), ]

# Check the matching: should print TRUE (every row lines up with its expression column)
all(covar$geoID == colnames(expr))

# Initial size of the data: number of probes and samples
dim(expr)
```

```{r build-data}
# The three genes from Submissions 1 and 2
gene_names <- c("LYN", "JAK2", "PTX3")

# Analysis data frame: one row per woman
dat <- data.frame(
  geoID   = covar$geoID,
  vitD    = covar$mat_vitD,                 # continuous covariate of interest
  age     = covar$mat_age_yrs,              # extra continuous covariate 1
  gestAge = covar$delivery_gestAge_wks,     # extra continuous covariate 2
  BMI     = covar$mat_BMI,
  outcome = factor(covar$preg_preeclampsia, levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia"))
)

# Derived categorical covariate: obesity status from BMI (obese = BMI >= 30 kg/m^2)
dat$obesity <- factor(ifelse(dat$BMI >= 30, "Obese", "Not obese"),
                      levels = c("Not obese", "Obese"))

# Add the expression of each gene as a column, using the probe-to-gene linker file
for (g in gene_names) {
  probe <- genes_link$PROBEID[genes_link$GENE == g][1]
  dat[[g]] <- as.numeric(expr[probe, ])
}

sum(is.na(dat))                    # should be 0: no samples removed
table(dat$outcome, dat$obesity)    # group sizes
```

```{r theme}
# One clean theme for all ggplot figures (no main title: figures are described in the legends)
theme_pub <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.title   = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text    = element_text(colour = "black"),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Colors used in every figure
col_main    <- "#0072B2"
col_obesity <- c("Not obese" = "#56B4E9", "Obese" = "#D55E00")
col_outcome <- c("Normal" = "#009E73", "Preeclampsia" = "#CC79A7")
```

# Table 1. Summary statistics

```{r table1}
# Helpers: mean (SD) and n (%) as text
mean_sd <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x), sd(x))
}
n_pct <- function(x, level) {
  sprintf("%d (%.1f)", sum(x == level), 100 * mean(x == level))
}

# Split the data by pregnancy outcome
normal <- dat[dat$outcome == "Normal", ]
pe     <- dat[dat$outcome == "Preeclampsia", ]

# Build the table one row at a time (LaTeX symbols are used in the row names)
tab <- data.frame(
  Variable = c("Maternal vitamin D (ng/mL), mean (SD)",
               "Maternal age (years), mean (SD)",
               "Gestational age at delivery (weeks), mean (SD)",
               "Obesity status, n (\\%)",
               "\\quad Not obese (BMI $<$ 30)",
               "\\quad Obese (BMI $\\geq$ 30)"),
  Normal = c(mean_sd(normal$vitD), mean_sd(normal$age), mean_sd(normal$gestAge),
             "", n_pct(normal$obesity, "Not obese"), n_pct(normal$obesity, "Obese")),
  Preeclampsia = c(mean_sd(pe$vitD), mean_sd(pe$age), mean_sd(pe$gestAge),
                   "", n_pct(pe$obesity, "Not obese"), n_pct(pe$obesity, "Obese")),
  Overall = c(mean_sd(dat$vitD), mean_sd(dat$age), mean_sd(dat$gestAge),
              "", n_pct(dat$obesity, "Not obese"), n_pct(dat$obesity, "Obese"))
)
names(tab) <- c("Variable",
                paste0("Normal (n = ", nrow(normal), ")"),
                paste0("Preeclampsia (n = ", nrow(pe), ")"),
                paste0("Overall (n = ", nrow(dat), ")"))

# LaTeX table; escape = FALSE keeps the LaTeX symbols; label gives \label{tab:summary}
table1 <- kable(tab, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, align = "lccc",
                label = "summary",
                caption = paste("Characteristics of the study participants",
                                "by pregnancy outcome. Continuous variables are",
                                "mean (standard deviation); categorical variables",
                                "are n (\\%)."))

# Save the table for Overleaf (\input{table1.tex}) and show it here
writeLines(table1, "table1.tex")
table1
```

# Figure 1. *LYN*: histogram, scatterplot and boxplot

```{r fig1, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
# Pearson correlation between vitamin D and LYN
ct <- cor.test(dat$vitD, dat$LYN)
r_txt <- sprintf("%.2f", ct$estimate)
p_txt <- ifelse(ct$p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", ct$p.value))

# Axis label with only the gene name in italics
lyn_lab <- bquote(italic("LYN") ~ "expression (log"[2] ~ "intensity)")

# (A) Histogram with a dashed line at the mean
p_hist <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = LYN)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = col_main, colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(dat$LYN), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = lyn_lab, y = "Number of women") +
  theme_pub

# (B) Scatterplot. The correlation label is placed above the highest point
#     so it cannot overlap any point.
label_y <- max(dat$LYN) + 0.20 * (max(dat$LYN) - min(dat$LYN))

p_scatter <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = vitD, y = LYN)) +
  geom_point(colour = col_main, alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black", fill = "grey70") +
  annotate("text", x = min(dat$vitD), y = label_y, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4,
           label = paste0("Pearson r = ", r_txt, ", p ", p_txt)) +
  labs(x = "Maternal vitamin D (ng/mL)", y = lyn_lab) +
  theme_pub

# (C) Boxplot by outcome and obesity with jittered points (random jitter: seed set above)
p_box <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = outcome, y = LYN, fill = obesity)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.7,
               position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8),
             size = 1.4, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_obesity, name = "Obesity status") +
  labs(x = "Pregnancy outcome", y = lyn_lab) +
  theme_pub

# Combine into one figure with panels A, B, C
top_row <- ggarrange(p_hist, p_scatter, ncol = 2, labels = c("A", "B"))
fig1 <- ggarrange(top_row, p_box, nrow = 2, labels = c("", "C"))
fig1

# Save for Overleaf
ggsave("figures/Figure1_LYN.pdf", fig1, width = 10, height = 8)
```

# Figure 2. Heatmap of ten genes

```{r heatmap-data}
# Genes: the 3 genes above + the 7 most variable named genes in the data
# (picking from the data guarantees that every gene exists and has no missing values)

# Gene name and standard deviation of every probe
probe_gene <- genes_link$GENE[match(rownames(expr), genes_link$PROBEID)]
probe_sd   <- apply(as.matrix(expr), 1, sd)

# Keep probes with a real gene name and some variation, that are not our 3 genes
ok <- !is.na(probe_gene) & probe_gene != "" & probe_gene != "---" &
      !is.na(probe_sd) & probe_sd > 0 &
      !(probe_gene %in% gene_names)

# Sort from most to least variable, keep one probe per gene, take the first 7
cand_probes  <- rownames(expr)[ok][order(probe_sd[ok], decreasing = TRUE)]
cand_genes   <- probe_gene[match(cand_probes, rownames(expr))]
extra_probes <- cand_probes[!duplicated(cand_genes)][1:7]
extra_genes  <- cand_genes[!duplicated(cand_genes)][1:7]

# Probes for our 3 genes + the 7 extra genes
main_probes <- genes_link$PROBEID[match(gene_names, genes_link$GENE)]
heat_genes  <- c(gene_names, extra_genes)
heat_probes <- c(main_probes, extra_probes)
heat_genes

# Expression matrix: genes in rows, women in columns
heat_mat <- as.matrix(expr[heat_probes, ])
rownames(heat_mat) <- heat_genes

# Tracking bars: one row per woman (row names = sample IDs)
annot <- data.frame(Outcome = dat$outcome, Obesity = dat$obesity)
rownames(annot) <- dat$geoID
annot_cols <- list(Outcome = col_outcome, Obesity = col_obesity)
```

```{r fig2, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.5}
hm <- pheatmap(heat_mat,
               scale = "row",                       # z-score each gene
               # clustering uses the defaults: Euclidean distance, complete linkage
               annotation_col = annot,              # tracking bars
               annotation_colors = annot_cols,
               show_colnames = FALSE,               # 157 sample IDs would be unreadable
               # italic gene names
               labels_row = parse(text = paste0("italic('", heat_genes, "')")),
               color = colorRampPalette(c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"))(100),
               border_color = NA,
               fontsize = 11)

# Save for Overleaf
ggsave("figures/Figure2_heatmap.pdf", hm$gtable, width = 10, height = 5.5)
```

# Figure 3. Dumbbell plot (additional plot type)

```{r fig3, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5}
# z-score each gene across all women so genes on different scales can be compared
z_mat <- t(scale(t(heat_mat)))

# Mean z-score of each gene in each outcome group
db <- data.frame(
  gene         = heat_genes,
  Normal       = rowMeans(z_mat[, dat$outcome == "Normal"]),
  Preeclampsia = rowMeans(z_mat[, dat$outcome == "Preeclampsia"])
)
db$diff <- db$Preeclampsia - db$Normal

# Order the genes by the difference (largest increase in preeclampsia at the top)
db$gene <- factor(db$gene, levels = db$gene[order(db$diff)])

# Long format for the two colored points
db_long <- data.frame(
  gene    = rep(db$gene, 2),
  outcome = factor(rep(c("Normal", "Preeclampsia"), each = nrow(db)),
                   levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
  mean_z  = c(db$Normal, db$Preeclampsia)
)

fig3 <- ggplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = db, aes(x = Normal, xend = Preeclampsia, y = gene, yend = gene),
               colour = "grey50", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = db_long, aes(x = mean_z, y = gene, colour = outcome), size = 3.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = col_outcome, name = "Pregnancy outcome") +
  labs(x = "Mean expression (z-score)", y = "Gene") +
  theme_pub +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"))   # italic gene names
fig3

# Save for Overleaf
ggsave("figures/Figure3_dumbbell.pdf", fig3, width = 7, height = 4.5)
```
